title: Weekly study
tomorrow: thirty minutes of silence a week. where would you even start?

lines: THE SQUARE BY THE WATER GATE.
cards: Buying an online course takes a click; finishing it is another matter. Here's a class that held a whole square until noon.
In Jerusalem, after the exile, the people gathered as one in the square before the water gate and asked Ezra the scribe to bring out the book of the law. He stood on a wooden platform.
When he opened the book, everyone stood up. He read from morning until midday, and they listened the whole time. And then they began to weep.

teach.b: Levites stood with the people, and the book of Nehemiah describes what they did: So they read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.
A reading, and teachers to explain it. Why the tears? The text doesn't say; some readers think the people were hearing how far they had drifted from it.
But the leaders stopped them: This day is holy unto the LORD your God; mourn not, nor weep. Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared.

teach.h: THE JOY OF THE LORD IS YOUR STRENGTH.
teach.b: And then: the joy of the LORD is your strength. That is the teaching. In Jewish tradition, study is a holy act, and here it ends at a table.
Tradition remembers Ezra among those who set the public reading of the Torah, and in synagogues it is read week by week, a portion at a time, the parashah, with teachers who give the sense.
Weekly study is that rhythm: a longer reading, someone to explain it, and joy at the end.

how: Jewish communities read the Torah aloud in synagogue on Shabbat, Mondays and Thursdays, a portion (parashah) each week, and study it with teachers and partners.

games.q: your study group finishes a hard passage and everyone feels low about how little they understood. what did the leaders tell Ezra's crowd?
o: don't weep: eat, drink and share, for the joy of the LORD is your strength.
keep weeping, since sorrow proves you took the reading seriously.
go home and study alone until you understand all of it.
games.why: the day of the reading was holy, so it ended in a meal shared with those who had nothing.

practice: Pick up a book you've meant to study, or bring to mind one class you could join. Write on the first page, by hand, the day and hour you'll come back to it each week.
Then read its first line once, slowly, and let it settle with your breathing.
